newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down on softer weekend cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down on softer weekend cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended broadly lower Friday in a moderate session, undermined by some follow-through long liquidation and profit taking in the face of further weakness in the cash, sources said.
June slipped 3.1 cents to close at $2.242 per million British thermal units. July settled 4.1 cents lower at $2.247. Other deferreds ended down by three to fourteen cents.

"We opened unchanged, then headed south. There was very heavy long liquidation again today, and next week we could see more fund rolling," said one Midwest trader, noting cash late this week finally showed some signs of weakness.

With Midwest and eastern temperatures expected to moderate next week, some agreed physical prices may fade further near-term, but few expected them to crumble, with steady injections and broader cooling loads likely later this month.

Technically, traders pegged support in June first at $2.195-2.20, with major buying likely at $2.05 and then along the up trendline around $2.04. Resistance was seen at the new high of $2.43 and then at $2.47-50.

In the cash, Gulf Coast weekend cash prices slipped by about a nickel Friday to the mid-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were down by about the same amount to the $2.04-09 range. New York city gate gas lost a few cents to the mid-$2.50s.
The NYMEX 12-month Hub strip tumbled 4.1 cents to $2.281. NYMEX said 43,325 contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 50,169.
On the KCBT, June finished 5.3 cents lower at $2.09, while deferreds ended down by four to 5.1 cents. The East/West spread widened by 2.2 cents to 15.2 cents (NYMEX premium). ((J
